VSS reports are delivered in an order based on several report characteristics.
This table lists the delivery order of VSS reports.
Processors determine what option to use for values placed in the Destination Identifier field in report records. When
the acquiring or issuing identifier identification option is selected, the report Destination Identifier is placed in the
Destination Identifier field of the machine-readable (TC 46) and print-ready (TC 47) report records. The acquiring or
issuing identifier identification option should be selected if the processor wants report records in acquiring or issuing
identifier sequence. If this option is not used, the Report Destination processor is placed in the Destination Identifier
field. The processor is always in the report records for summary-level SREs.
Daily reports are delivered first. On the first processing day of each month, monthly reports for the previous month
are delivered after the daily reports.

Machine-readable (TC 46) records are organized by VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) report.
Each report line of data has one or two records, depending on the transaction format used.
Common report information appears in the first record for each report line of data. If a second
record is required, the common report information is not included in that record. The
transaction format used for the machine-readable record depends on the report.
Each record begins with a “46” (positions 1 and 2), and all reports belong to Report Group V
(position 59). There are nine (9) different transaction formats, identified by the Report Subgroup
(position 60). All transaction formats consist of one transaction component record (TCR), except
for Report Subgroups 4, 6, and 9, which consist of two TCRs. The TCR is identified in Transaction
Single Message System (SMS)-connected clients using a Direct Access Service (DAS) VisaNet
Access Point (VAP) for report delivery receive the machine-readable records in the file type of
SMS-connected clients using non-VAP delivery receive the machine-readable records as a
separate transmission. There is no header or trailer record.
BASE II-connected clients and SMS-connected clients using a BASE II VAP receive the machine-
readable records in their Center Transaction File (CTF)—Incoming Interchange.

The four levels of reporting entities are:
The funds transfer SRE is the level at which funds transfer occurs. The funds transfer SRE can be at any level in the VSS hierarchy.
A processor is a Visa endpoint (or Visa-approved third-party) that provides authorization, clearing, or settlement services for
merchants and clients. The processor captures transactions counts and amounts online. A running total of counts and amounts is
accumulated every 30 minutes. The system stores these totals as advice messages (0520) for recovery by the processor.

The SMS transaction detail reports (SMS600–SMS617) cumulatively reflect all of a client's interchange transactions for one processing
The reports assist the client center to reconcile its position with the V.I.P. System by providing a detailed transaction listing for the
issuer or acquirer at the affiliate ID level. Subtotals are provided for each affiliate ID. Reports also generate a subtotal and force a
page-break any time a client reporting level changes. For example, if one affiliate ID has activity with two processors, the report will
have two affiliate subtotals—one for each processor.
Reports are produced daily for delivery to the subscriber. Subscription is optional for all transaction detail reports.
The SMS exception detail reports (SMS610–SMS617) are a subset of the transaction detail reports. Exception detail reports display a
particular category of the client's exception transactions for one processing day.
These transactions are also displayed on the SMS600 or SMS601 report. Exception detail reports have the same functionality and
fields as the SMS600 and SMS601 reports.
